# Pending-request reset and recovery comparison

Predeclared focused comparison for #3142, A1/A2 main 551d4d0825dca64b7143d6f18fc2b13baaf1fe0a and B 7a28f823bc8bc684a782cfdfd91c7e11882d6da2. Sequential A1/B/A2 on one ubuntu-latest VM, same compiled fixture and exact product/dependency replacements. Both revisions build and pass fixture validation before timing. Retain the existing simple rent/return benchmark and add completed-response/reset/recovery cases with and without a reservation disposal exception.

Each recovery operation completes and consumes one response, returns that request through reservation cleanup, then completes and returns a second request. A failed reset must propagate the original exception once, destroy the failed request, and allow successful replacement use. Successful reset must reuse the same request. A library protocol writer constructs the common response frame before measurement. The frame and reservation/exception fixtures are reused; all allocations caused by throwing, discarded requests and replacement creation remain measured. These are per-request fault/recovery costs, not per-message zero-allocation claims. The successful reset path and separate basic rent/return benchmark are expected to allocate 0 B after warmup.

The only correctness adaptation is an explicit baseline assertion for main's known count defect: after N failed resets its count is 1-N, while the candidate must remain 1 after successful recovery. This counter is not used to control work. Both revisions must complete identical operations, preserve exception identity and dispose the reservation exactly once per operation. Do not normalize the defect away or infer baseline correctness from timing success.

Every fresh process executes each case continuously for at least 20 seconds before BDN's 30 workload warmup iterations, followed by 25 measured iterations of approximately one second, DontRemove and MemoryDiagnoser. Tiered compilation is disabled identically to isolate steady machine-code costs; runtime boundaries and named JIT events remain recorded. Record actual elapsed warmup, completed operations, CPU, allocations, GC, heap/RSS and thread-pool changes. Preserve exact binary hashes and full sources. Declare a 3% mean-time/control-drift screen and no allocation increase for each like-for-like case against both controls. These focused screens cannot establish per-message p50/p99/max or end-to-end CPU and stability.

The prior loaded fixed-heap comparison 34301881559 remains INCONCLUSIVE because of maximum control drift, runtime transitions and missing default DATAS/fault coverage. This new fault-path experiment is not an identical repeat and does not waive those conditions or automatically pass the PR gate. It closes the missing isolated reset/recovery measurement; a full acceptance decision still requires applicable protected metrics and fresh-head coverage.
